findings.issue_text: All 5 lenses returned and both high-impact claims verified. Consolidated results:

Manifest verdict NEEDS_REVISION — "missing shard result for shard-01"; shard-01 is the ENTIRE 31-file diff, so no reviewer output was actually produced, yet the run reports PASS_ADVISORY with 4/4 reviewers PASS and 0 findings. The PASS is vacuous.
Risk level scored "none" for a diff that adds a credential-writing webhook, symmetric decryption, and team authorization logic — the profiler is miscalibrated for this change class.
Runtime assessment: "static-only; runtime not assessed" — none of the credential-sync paths were executed.
PASS with 0 findings despite zero test changes and no validation evidence accompanying a new public API endpoint and 7 rewired OAuth integrations.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update` called but `prisma` is never imported (imports end at line 20). Build failure / `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce service construction — the integration is entirely broken, not just the sync path.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` sits AFTER the `if (state?.teamId) {...return}` block, so it is only reachable with `teamId: null`. The team-credential write at line 47 is guarded solely by an accepted-membership query (line 32) with no role filter. Privilege boundary for team credentials silently downgraded ADMIN/OWNER → MEMBER across the 6 callbacks using this helper.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `key` receives the zod `safeParse` wrapper `{success, data}` (helper returns the wrapper, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29) and is written straight to `credential.key` at line 100; previously it held `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`. After the first refresh the credential becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}` and line 75 throws forever — permanently bricked.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:50 — `prisma.app.findUnique` selects only `slug` (line 42), a value already in `reqBody.appSlug`, then indexes `appStoreMetadata` by that slug. The DB round-trip is a no-op, which is the tell that it should select `dirName`; `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory. Returns 404 for exactly the apps this change wires up whose dirName ≠ slug (google-calendar/googlecalendar, msteams/office365video, lark-calendar/larkcalendar, office365-calendar/office365calendar).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — the `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` placeholder is applied unconditionally, including the NON-sync branch. Office 365's schema declares `refresh_token: z.string().optional()` (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:56), so any Microsoft response omitting a rotated token spreads the literal string over the stored credential at line 264, destroying the user's real refresh token on ordinary self-hosted/cloud installs.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — both computed keys (lines 8 and 10) evaluate to the same literal `"[object Object]"`; the later overwrites the former. Neither documented behaviour exists, and `z.object` strip-mode drops `expires_in`/`expiry_date`/`instance_url` — synced tokens are persisted with no expiry.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — returns a raw `fetch` Response on the sync branch but the provider-specific object otherwise, with no `response.ok` check and `refreshFunction: () => any` defeating type checking. Two structurally incompatible return shapes; a failing sync endpoint (404/500) is handed to callers as a successful token response.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — `res?.data` assumes a Gaxios response; on the sync path it is a `fetch` Response with no `.data`, so line 95 throws a TypeError swallowed by the catch at line 103 (message ≠ "invalid_grant"). Refresh silently no-ops and the expired token keeps being used.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — result annotated `: HubspotToken` but is a `Response` on the sync path; `expiresIn` is undefined → `expiryDate` NaN (line 192), the Response is persisted as `credential.key` (line 198), and `setAccessToken(undefined)` runs (line 202). Catch at line 203 only logs.

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88 — adopted `refreshOAuthTokens` but not `parseRefreshTokenResponse`; still validates with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires literal `scope`/`token_type`, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`. The sync endpoint's documented minimal response can never satisfy it — Webex refresh always rejects once sync is on.

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84 — same half-migration; the result is piped through `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` and read as Lark's nested `{code,msg,data}` envelope. Under sync the credential is overwritten with `undefined` refresh_token and NaN expiries rather than failing loudly.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — no `parseRefreshTokenResponse`; the whole response body replaces `credential.key`, dropping `refresh_token` permanently. Its near-identical sibling office365calendar does use the helper — same vendor, two implementations.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — adopted `parseRefreshTokenResponse` but hand-rolls a raw `fetch` instead of `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce is excluded from credential sync while still being validated against the minimal sync schema. It also adds an unconditional token POST + DB write on every service construction (constructor, line 57) with no expiry check.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:106 — the `jsforce.Connection` is built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`, not the token just fetched and persisted at lines 88-99. The added round-trip buys nothing.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92 — `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` is unreachable: the helper throws at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:22 on failure and never returns a failed result. Same dead check at office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — sync predicate omits the `&& userId` condition its counterpart has at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5. For team credentials (`userId === null`) the token is refreshed against the real provider but validated with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, stripping all fields and substituting the placeholder refresh token.
Endpoint hardening and error handling**
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — no HTTP method check; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the credential write path.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — bare `schema.parse()` with no try/catch or error boundary; malformed bodies surface as 500 + stack trace instead of 400.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` both unguarded, and the key falls back to `""` when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset. No "encryption key not configured" precondition despite the feature depending on it.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — the secret comparison never asserts `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is non-empty, so an unset secret plus an absent header satisfies `undefined !== undefined`. CAVEAT: reachability depends on how `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined in `@calcom/lib/constants`, which is outside this 30-file slice and could not be verified — treat as hardening, not a confirmed bypass.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — existing-credential lookup is `findFirst({userId, appId})` with no `teamId` filter and no ordering; overwrites an arbitrary one of the user's credentials for that app.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — attacker-controlled `req.query.state` goes to a bare `JSON.parse` with no try/catch and is type-asserted with no runtime validation; the unvalidated `teamId` then flows into `prisma.credential.create` as the owner (createOAuthAppCredential.ts:51).

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — the outbound POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no secret or signature, while the inbound half of the same seam requires a shared secret. Asymmetric trust boundary.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 — the diff deleted the `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", ...)` block and changed semantics from log-and-continue to throw, with nothing replacing the diagnostic.

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `${appConfig.slug}` replaced with a hardcoded `zoho-bigin` inside a now-pointless template literal, while line 12 still uses `appConfig.slug` and line 22 `appConfig.scope`. Unrelated to all four stated goals; slug and redirect URI can now diverge.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/callback.ts:44 (also office365calendar/api/callback.ts:68, larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:70) — hand-rolled `prisma.credential.create` with hardcoded `userId`, ignoring `state.teamId`, while 6 sibling callbacks route through `createOAuthAppCredential`. NOTE: PRE-EXISTING — I verified these hunks are imports-only, so this is an integration-shape gap the new helper did not close, not a regression introduced here.

Two notes on the run itself. First, `docs/tasks/task-001.md` was flagged by the intent lens as an artifact shipped under `docs/` — I'm not counting it as a finding: the `task` commit that carried it no longer exists in the repo and the file is untracked, so it's a harness artifact. Second, related: HEAD moved from `35e9776` to `e58c326` during the run and `HEAD~2` is no longer a valid revision. I captured the full diff before that happened and disk state equals the `pr` commit, so every `file:line` above was verified against the code under review.

The headline: the deterministic gate returned PASS_ADVISORY on a diff that does not compile (missing `prisma` import), permanently corrupts Google Calendar credentials on first refresh, and downgrades team-credential authorization from admin to member — because its only shard produced no result and the PASS was recorded anyway.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file) returns a `fetch(...)` `Response` object on the credential-sync path (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — sync predicate omits the `&& userId` condition its counterpart has at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5. For team credentials (`userId === null`) the token is refreshed against the real provider but validated with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, stripping all fields and substituting the placeholder refresh token.
Endpoint hardening and error handling**

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new webhook API route (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) that is not hardened and has weak error handling: it does not restrict HTTP methods (so GET/PUT/etc. will be processed), and it uses `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` plus `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` without any try/catch. Any invalid/missing body, missing/invalid encryption key (`CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` defaults to ""), bad ciphertext, or non-JSON plaintext will throw and result in an unhandled 500 instead of a controlled 4xx response. These are concrete, verifiable issues in the added endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — no HTTP method check; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the credential write path.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the `handler` function does not check `req.method` anywhere. After the feature-flag and webhook-secret header checks, it unconditionally parses `req.body` with Zod and then performs Prisma reads/writes (`credential.update` / `credential.create`). Therefore, any HTTP method (GET/PUT/DELETE/etc.) that reaches this handler with the correct header/secret and a compatible request body can trigger the credential write path; there is no restriction to POST-only behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same issue: using `schema.parse()` without handling parse errors causes invalid payloads to throw and return 500 responses (possibly with stack traces) instead of a proper 400 Bad Request. This matches the golden comment’s concern about client confusion and incorrect error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` both unguarded, and the key falls back to `""` when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset. CAVEAT: reachability depends on how `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined in `@calcom/lib/constants`, which is outside this 30-file slice and could not be verified — treat as hardening, not a confirmed bypass.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — existing-credential lookup is `findFirst({userId, appId})` with no `teamId` filter and no ordering; overwrites an arbitrary one of the user's credentials for that app.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the code looks up an existing credential via prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } }) and then updates that single record. Using findFirst without an orderBy means the chosen credential is nondeterministic if more than one credential exists for the same (userId, appId) pair (which is plausible given the use of findFirst rather than findUnique). That would cause the webhook to overwrite an arbitrary credential for that app for the user. The diff does not apply any additional disambiguation (e.g., teamId or credential id), so the risk described is present in the introduced code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, performs a POST to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no shared secret header, signature, etc.). This creates a verifiable asymmetry: the “push into Cal.com” path is authenticated, while the “pull/refresh via external endpoint” path is unauthenticated as implemented here, which is a real security/trust-boundary issue unless external protections exist (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The headline: the deterministic gate returned PASS_ADVISORY on a diff that does not compile (missing `prisma` import), permanently corrupts Google Calendar credentials on first refresh, and downgrades team-credential authorization from admin to member — because its only shard produced no result and the PASS was recorded anyway.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces a real correctness bug in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: it now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and writes `{ key }` to Prisma. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed credential payload itself. This would store the wrong shape into `credential.key` (effectively corrupting the stored credentials on refresh). 

However, other parts of the proposed finding are not supported by the diff: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` *does* import `prisma`, and the diff shown does not demonstrate any “downgrade” of team-credential authorization logic—only import path changes for `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam`.
